evidence.positive: Against the shipped build (ff735801d) in tenant mayo-mayo: created an adult patient (53.3 kg, 170 cm) and an in-progress appendectomy case via the admin API, set the Intralipid ERX 40840090 client mapping concentration to 20%, then injected a RAS^O17 bolus of 16 g Intralipid (RXA-6/7 = 16 g, RXR IV) via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send. Log: 'Found 1 default dose adjustments for AdjustmentService.SearchQuery(... medicationIdentifier=m-intralipid, weightClass=NORMAL)', 'Rule evaluated: w-default-dose-adjustment -> true', then 'Persisted HL7-sourced MedicationAdministration id=01a0ef0c-90a4-...'. DB: medication_administrations row 16 g (tracking 01a0ef0c-90cc-...), rule_fired_results w-default-dose-adjustment with route_default_dose_override INTRAVENOUS calculatedLabel '80 mL' (1.5 mL/kg x 53.3 kg), and compliance_results default-dose compliant=t. So a gram-charted dose is now converted through the 20% concentration (80 mL = 16 g) and compared, instead of throwing.
evidence.negative: Same setup, injected 50 g Intralipid (sequence 2). Log shows the same w-default-dose-adjustment firing and 'Persisted HL7-sourced MedicationAdministration id=01a0ef0c-e012-...'. DB: medication_administrations row 50 g, rule_fired_results override calculatedLabel '80 mL', compliance_results compliant=f. This proves the comparison genuinely runs after unit conversion (50 g = 250 mL is outside the 80 mL +/- 10 mL band) rather than the evaluator defaulting every gram dose to compliant, and the administration is still saved when non-compliant. Repeated after the class restore (sequences 4 and 5): 16 g -> compliant=t, 50 g -> compliant=f, both persisted.
evidence.red_check: Compiled pre-fix variants inside the container (javac against /app/resources:/app/classes:/app/libs/*): the parent-commit DefaultDoseComplianceEvaluator (raw isGreaterThanOrEqualTo on unconverted doses), plus the shipped RuleComplianceService and RuleExecutionResultService with only the OR-2931 hunks reverted (public evaluateCompliance, needsAction.forEach(ruleComplianceService::evaluateCompliance), @Slf4j replaced by an explicit logger). Backed up the four shipped .class files (md5 recorded), copied the pre-fix classes into /app/classes, docker restart. Injected 50 g Intralipid (sequence 3): log went red with 'HL7 processor MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessor failed for type=RAS^O17' and 'com.guided.orci.exceptions.IncomparableException: Doses are incomparable. MassBasedDose[quantity=50 g] cannot be compared to VolumeBasedDose[quantity=70 ml] due to incompatible units' with the exact Sentry frames (Dose.java:57 -> isWithinWeightBasedRange:64 -> isMedAdminCompliantWithDose:50 -> evaluate:109 -> RuleComplianceService.evaluateCompliance). medication_administrations stayed at 2 rows and rule_fired_results at 2, i.e. the RAS administration and its firing were lost exactly as the ticket describes. Restored the four backed-up classes, md5sums in the container matched the backup for all four, restarted, and re-ran 16 g and 50 g: both persisted with compliant=t / compliant=f and no exception.

caveats: The Intralipid ERX client mapping had no concentration locally (concentrations = []); it was set to 20% by SQL so the gram-to-volume conversion could be exercised. Without a concentration the fix scores the pair compliant by design (covered by the unit test testWeightBasedCompliantWhenAdministeredMassCannotBeConvertedToExpectedVolume), which was not separately observed at runtime.

The per-firing try/catch in evaluateComplianceForFirings was not independently provoked at runtime: with the fix no evaluator throws in this scenario. Its guard is covered by the new RuleExecutionResultServiceTest.evaluatorFailure_doesNotRollBackTheSaveOrCostOtherFirings.
The red-check DefaultDoseComplianceEvaluator was the parent-commit version, which also predates the OR-2945 insulin default-dose change; that path is unrelated to the Intralipid scenario exercised.

SingleMin/SingleMax dose compliance evaluators and the indication default-dose path also changed in this PR but were not exercised at runtime; they share the same isDoseCompliant helper and have new unit tests.
Only the Mayo RAS ingestion path was exercised; the user-charted (UI) administration path into the same evaluator was not.

automation.assessment: The PR added thorough unit coverage: DefaultDoseComplianceEvaluatorTest (gram vs mL/kg conversion, rounding band edges, no-concentration fallback, indication weight-based default), SingleMin/SingleMax evaluator tests, DoseTest.isComparableTo, and RuleExecutionResultServiceTest proving a throwing evaluator no longer rolls back the save. Nothing in qa-suite or mayo-client-integration exercises RAS -> compliance end to end, and MayoHL7RasMedAdminProcessorTest does not cover the compliance scoring. Worth locking in one integration-level case that reproduces the production shape (RAS gram dose against a weight-based mL/kg default adjustment) so a future evaluator regression cannot silently drop administrations again.
proposed_tests: mayo-client-integration or orci Spring integration test: RAS Intralipid bolus in g for a NORMAL-weight adult with the m-intralipid 1.5 mL/kg default_dose adjustment and a 20% mapping concentration -> administration persisted, w-default-dose-adjustment fired, compliance_results default-dose compliant=true at 16 g and false at 50 g
Same harness with an empty mapping concentration: gram dose persists and scores compliant (incomparable pair -> no usable guidance), asserting no IncomparableException reaches HL7MessageDispatcher

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A Mayo RAS Intralipid bolus charted as 16 g against the 1.5 mL/kg default was persisted and scored default-dose compliant after conversion through the 20% concentration.
Negative: The same bolus at 50 g was persisted and scored non-compliant, so the unit-converted comparison genuinely runs instead of defaulting to compliant.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix compliance classes into the running app reproduced the Sentry IncomparableException stack trace and dropped the administration; the shipped classes were restored and re-verified.

Automation: Unit coverage from the PR is thorough; one integration-level RAS gram-dose test is proposed to lock in the end-to-end shape.
